details:
SPHEREx Explorer is a web application I developed as a solo participant for the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge. It makes real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations easier to explore and compare across dates and wavelengths.

Try the application: https://spherex-explorer-l9m4r.ondigitalocean.app/
Code: https://github.com/Snikerso/spherex-explorer/tree/app-platform-release
Me: https://www.drojecki.pro/

Key features:

  • Search by sky coordinates, date, and archive release.
  • Retrieve real observations from NASA/IPAC IRSA.
  • Align images and compare them using animation or synchronized side-by-side views.
  • Create false-color RGB images and detector stacks.
  • Explore point measurements across wavelengths and differences between observations.
  • Use a natural-language copilot alongside manual controls.
  • Inspect observation metadata, save notes, and export images, videos, and measurement tables.
  • Explore a 3D mission view with orbital context.

I built the application using React, TypeScript, NestJS, MongoDB, Python, Astropy, and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Its main creative feature is a copilot that shares the user’s controls, making exploration approachable while preserving manual control.

My goal is to help students and astronomy enthusiasts investigate infrared data without building their own processing pipeline. Dates, wavelengths, and sources remain visible because apparent changes may reflect wavelength differences or processing effects. The application supports exploration and follow-up, rather than claiming confirmed detections or a discovery of Planet X.
